newsitem.title: UK: London musical "Always" closes after bad reviews.
newsitem.headline: London musical "Always" closes after bad reviews.

text.p: The writing was on the wall from the moment "Always" was nicknamed "Briefly" by dismissive London reviewers.
On Tuesday the Australian musical featuring British king Edward VIII's ill-fated 1930s romance with Wallis Simpson lived down to its reviews and closed after just six weeks.
Costing three million pounds ($5 million) to stage, Always had to run 24 weeks to recoup its cost. But it was panned and the audiences stayed away.
"Do any of us need the stress of this show in our lives?" asked the Independent newspaper.
"If Never were a place, you'd want to take it there. In terms of run, I suspect that Always will have to be renamed Briefly."
Others called it banal, bland and repetitive and heritage kitsch. One accused it of "buttock-clenching comic awfulness".
"We are delighted that our audiences have greatly enjoyed the production and are very sad that we are closing earlier than anticipated," the producers said in a statement.

London's theatreland is packed with musicals -- there are 17 running at present, filling about half the West End theatres. But only top-class American imports and shows produced by Sir Andrew Lloyd Webber or Cameron Mackintosh are surefire winners.
In 1992 a Norwegian musical Which Witch?, about a young girl denounced as a witch who falls in love with a bishop, closed after 10 weeks after a savaging from critics.
"They should have stuck to herring boats," one said.
